item.content:encoded:
Dhangadhi, August 20

A member of a school management committee has been arrested in Kailali while accepting a bribe of Rs 200,000.

The person arrested is Dev Bahadur Bam, a member of the management committee of Kalika Secondary School in Gaurigunga Municipality-4.

The Commission for the Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) office in Mahendranagar said a team it had deployed caught Bam red-handed with the bribe money on Thursday.

According to Mahendranagar CIAA information officer Chetraj Bhatta, Bam had collected the money after luring a school staff member with the promise of increasing their salary.

The CIAA said Bam has been taken into custody for further questioning and investigation.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

A two-and-a-half-year-old boy who had been missing for two days in a community forest east of Nawalparasi has been rescued safely. Shiwan Tamang, two and a half, went missing from Gaindakot Municipality-14, Bhagar, in eastern Nawalparasi, and was found safe in a community forest two days later.

At 7 am on August 18, Shiwan’s grandmother, Hem Kumari Ale, had gone to the Shankhadevi Community Forest near their home to pick mushrooms. When she returned home, Shiwan was not there.

After residents and neighbours searched the forest area without finding him, they filed a report at the Area Police Office.

Teams from the Area Police Office Gaindakot, Area Police Office Rajahar, and a temporary police post at Beldiya were mobilised alongside residents to search for Shiwan.

During the search, Shiwan was found at 10 am on Thursday near the head of the Bhagar stream, within the Shankhadevi Community Forest in Gaindakot Municipality-14.

Police said the boy, rescued safely, was handed over to relatives after completing the necessary procedures.

item.dc:creator: Shashwat Pant
item.description:
Kathmandu, August 20 International visitors to Nepal can now use their existing Mastercard credit and debit cards to make digital payments at merchants accepting NepalPay and Fonepay QR codes nationwide. Mastercard on Wednesday announced the launch of its Pay Local solution in Nepal in partnership with MOCO, a card-based digital wallet and unified QR payment […]

The post Mastercard, MOCO launch QR payment solution for international visitors in Nepal appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

International visitors to Nepal can now use their existing Mastercard credit and debit cards to make digital payments at merchants accepting NepalPay and Fonepay QR codes nationwide.

Mastercard on Wednesday announced the launch of its Pay Local solution in Nepal in partnership with MOCO, a card-based digital wallet and unified QR payment platform.

Under the new service, international travellers can link eligible Mastercard cards to the MOCO Travel App and make payments directly through the app without having to carry cash, exchange currency or load money into prepaid accounts.

The MOCO Travel App is available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

The service can be used at hotels, restaurants, retail outlets, local markets and other tourism-related businesses accepting NepalPay and Fonepay QR payments.

“International travellers increasingly expect the simplicity, security and convenience of their everyday payment experiences to travel with them,” said Sandun Hapugoda, country manager for Sri Lanka, Maldives, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal at Mastercard.

“With Mastercard Pay Local available on MOCO, visitors can use the cards they already know and trust across the country’s extensive QR payment ecosystem,” he said.

Mastercard said the service will also allow local businesses to serve international customers through their existing QR infrastructure, potentially helping them benefit from Nepal’s growing tourism sector.

The launch expands Mastercard’s Pay Local presence in Asia, following similar deployments in China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia and Sri Lanka.

Pranaya Rajbhandari, chief executive officer of FOCUSONE Payment Solutions, said the partnership would make it easier for inbound tourists to access Nepal’s QR payment ecosystem.

“Through our travel app, inbound tourists can seamlessly access Nepal’s QR payment ecosystem, making it easier to explore the country while supporting local merchants,” Rajbhandari said.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

Nepal’s stock market rose on Thursday after declining for four consecutive trading days.

The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) index gained 7.17 points to close at 2,629 points. The market had fallen by 0.26 points on Wednesday.

The index dropped to an intraday low of 2,608 points at around 12:23 pm before recovering steadily through the rest of the trading session.

Turnover also increased. A total of Rs 4.40 billion worth of shares changed hands on Thursday, compared with Rs 3.29 billion on Wednesday.

Shares of 132 companies gained while 132 declined. Prices of 13 companies remained unchanged.

Most sectoral indices recorded movements of less than 1%.

The hydropower index posted the biggest gain, rising 0.99%. Banking gained 0.28%, investment 0.05%, life insurance 0.01%, manufacturing and processing 0.76%, and the ‘Others’ group 0.09%.

Development banks declined 0.37%, finance companies 0.19%, hotels and tourism 0.05%, microfinance 0.06%, non-life insurance 0.48% and trading 0.21%.

The post Mobile app launched to track public transport in Kathmandu Valley appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

The KTM Public Transport mobile application has been launched to help passengers track public vehicles operating in Kathmandu Valley and check how long a vehicle will take to reach their location.

Sunita Dangol, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City and chairperson of the Federal Capital Urban Area Public Transport Council, launched the app at the council’s third meeting on Wednesday.

The application currently provides information on around 1,200 GPS-equipped public vehicles, with plans to expand the system to cover more vehicles.

Dangol said public transport in the Valley should be made simpler, more accessible and convenient. She stressed the need to expand night-time services and operate buses from early morning to accommodate students travelling to schools and colleges.

“Public transport is not an issue that can be confined to a single municipality. Since it connects different municipalities, it is a shared issue,” she said, calling for greater coordination among local governments.

The council has also approved programs to determine bus stops and pick-and-drop points, introduce night bus services, install GPS-based public transport information systems at major bus stops and bus parks, and prepare a legal framework for cashless fares.

The council also plans campaigns to encourage passengers to obtain tickets and studies aimed at improving public transport services.

The council has 35 members and a nine-member steering committee to streamline its decision-making process.

item.title: Parliamentary committee directs govt to reform foreign aid management
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Pant
item.description:
Kathmandu, August 20 The Public Accounts Committee of the House of Representatives has directed the government to introduce policy and institutional reforms to ensure foreign aid is mobilised in line with the principle of results-oriented spending. A meeting of the committee held at Singha Durbar on Thursday directed the government to ensure that foreign aid […]

The post Parliamentary committee directs govt to reform foreign aid management appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Public Accounts Committee of the House of Representatives has directed the government to introduce policy and institutional reforms to ensure foreign aid is mobilised in line with the principle of results-oriented spending.

A meeting of the committee held at Singha Durbar on Thursday directed the government to ensure that foreign aid in the coming days is aligned with national priorities, the budget system, public funds, transparency, auditing and results-based spending.

The committee also directed the government to bring all forms of foreign aid— whether cash, in-kind or technical — into the national budget system and government treasury as far as possible and subject them to mandatory auditing.

Committee Chair Bharat Bahadur Khadka said the Ministry of Finance had been instructed to include and allocate foreign-funded resources in the annual budget only after the availability of the assistance had been confirmed.

The ministry was also directed to ensure timely reimbursement of expenses made through foreign aid to minimise the additional financial burden on the government’s domestic resources caused by delays.

The committee called for an integrated record of foreign aid commitments, actual receipts, expenditure, utilisation and reimbursements, with mandatory updates in the relevant government systems.

It also directed the government to strengthen management, monitoring and implementation capacity so that projects funded through foreign aid are completed within their stipulated time and cost.

Speaking at the meeting, Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle said the ministry was closely monitoring the global economic situation, the effectiveness of foreign aid and new financial strategies Nepal should adopt.

Wagle said donor countries were increasingly imposing stricter conditions on aid or seeking to spend the funds through their own mechanisms to prevent misuse of taxpayers’ money.

Traditional sources of foreign aid, he said, were no longer sufficient or effective, prompting Nepal to explore alternative sources of financing.

The finance minister said alternative financing sources had already been given policy priority in the national budget and that the government was working to manage the transitional period while adapting to the changing global economic order.

The post Seriously injured Nepali in Poland awaits rescue appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Khotang, August 20

The family of a Nepali youth seriously injured in a road accident in Poland has accused the government of failing to take adequate steps to bring him back to Nepal.

Amitkumar Chaudhary of Itahari Sub-Metropolitan City-16, Sunsari, was seriously injured in a road accident in Poland. His family said the Nepal government has shown little concern about his rescue and repatriation.

According to his family, Chaudhary went to Poland three years ago for foreign employment. He was seriously injured in a road accident on Baisakh 5 and is currently receiving treatment at the Regional Hospital in Sosnowiec City, Poland, according to Parsuram Dhimal, who is in Poland.

Chaudhary’s wife, Usha Chaudhary, appealed to the Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) Poland for assistance on Ashadh 19. She said she had repeatedly requested help from the Foreign Employment Board, Ministry of Labour and Ministry of Foreign Affairs, but the government had not responded adequately.

Usha said the family’s financial situation does not allow them to cover the costs of repatriation, including airfare, which forced her to seek help from the NRNA.

Lawmaker Ashok Kumar Chaudhary had also raised the issue in Parliament, but the family said the government has yet to respond.

Meanwhile, NRNA Poland has started collecting donations to bring Chaudhary back to Nepal through the “Bring Amitkumar Chaudhary Home” campaign.

item.content:encoded:
Baitadi, August 20

A landslide has been continuously occurring in the Ratapani settlement of Surnaya Rural Municipality-8 in Baitadi, putting the entire settlement at risk. Six families have already been displaced, while 19 other houses remain at risk.

Resident Tej Bohara said the landslide has been occurring continuously for the past week.

“The landslide has been occurring continuously. Twenty-five families are living in fear,” he said. “So far, six families have been displaced. The displaced families are taking shelter with their neighbours.”

The landslide has damaged maize crops planted across around 25 to 30 ropanis of land. It has also disrupted the movement of students and residents.

“Landslides occur almost every day, and it is frightening even to walk around. The fear increases whenever it rains,” said resident Ramsingh Bohara.

Surnaya Rural Municipality Chairperson Ammar Bahadur Kunwar said the Ratapani settlement, which is at high risk from landslides, needs to be relocated.

“The landslide has been troubling this area for a long time, and the situation has worsened recently,” he said. “There is no alternative to relocating the settlement. We are coordinating with the relevant authorities.”

Neupane raised the questions during a meeting of the parliamentary committee […]

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) lawmaker Yagyamani Neupane has questioned the moral grounds of Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA) Chief Commissioner Prem Kumar Rai to continue in office, citing his alleged links to several controversial cases and court rulings.

Neupane raised the questions during a meeting of the parliamentary committee attended by Rai and other CIAA officials.

Referring to the Supreme Court’s ruling on the wide-body aircraft procurement case, Neupane said the court had mentioned that the procurement process for two wide-body aircraft had moved forward following a decision of the Nepal Airlines Corporation board chaired by Rai, who was then secretary at the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation.

Neupane questioned why Rai was not made a defendant in the case despite his name being mentioned in connection with the procurement process.

He argued that prosecuting some officials involved in the same process while not prosecuting others amounted to selective prosecution.

“Selective prosecution is contrary to the principle of equal justice, the right to equality and the principle of natural justice,” Neupane said.

He also raised questions about Rai’s alleged involvement in the Nepal Oil Corporation land acquisition case, saying that the parliamentary Public Accounts Committee had specifically mentioned Rai’s name. He also referred to issues surrounding Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa.

Neupane then brought up the fake Bhutanese refugee scam, saying he had obtained court documents in his capacity as a lawyer in the case.

Reading from the statement of accused Sanu Bhandari, Neupane alleged that Bhandari had claimed that then-secretary Prem Kumar Rai’s vehicle was used to deliver Rs 10 million in cash and that Rai later called him to his office.

According to the statement read out by Neupane, Bhandari claimed Rai told him that his work would be done and asked him to leave.

Neupane said these issues raised serious questions about Rai’s ethical grounds for continuing as CIAA chief.

“On this basis, Chief Commissioner, do you have the moral grounds to remain in office? Does the law allow you to continue in that position? This is my second question. I want an answer,” Neupane said.

item.content:encoded:
Furious residents have shut down rural roads within Jitpursimara Sub-Metropolitan City in Bara to protest the murder of three-year-old Garima Chaudhary following her rape.

Private and community schools within Jitpursimara Sub-Metropolitan City held mourning assemblies and closed on Thursday.

Calling the brutal incident against the three-year-old girl a shock to the entire education sector, private and community schools issued a statement demanding the strictest possible action against those responsible.

Protesters, saying police failed to act in time and that this led to the girl’s murder, continued their agitation today, which began on Wednesday.

Protesters have been burning tyres and demonstrating on rural roads within the sub-metropolitan city since early Thursday morning. Traffic on the Birgunj-Pathalaiya road section, closed since Wednesday afternoon, has still not resumed.

Locals accuse the Area Police Office of serious negligence in the search for Garima. They allege that although her father filed a report at the Simara Area Police Office in time after she went missing, police failed to show urgency in the search.

Locals are now protesting, demanding action against DSP Dilip Chhetri, in-charge of the Simara Area Police Office.

Surrounding the Area Police Office in Simara, protesters put forward their demand for action against DSP Chhetri.

Protesters, burning tyres, have completely halted traffic on the Simara-Dumarwana, Piluwa-Wadaharwa, Simara-Jitpur and Pathalaiya-Simara road sections within Jitpursimara Sub-Metropolitan City.

The Bara District Administration has said it remains positive about addressing the protesters’ demands and is attempting dialogue.

Chief District Officer Dharmendra Mishra said preparations were underway for decisive talks later today to address the protesters’ demands.

“We have already arrested the accused. As for the allegations of police negligence raised by locals, we are verifying that ourselves,” CDO Mishra said.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

CPN-UML leader Mohammad Ishtiyaq Rayi has proposed inviting Prime Minister Balen Shah to a parliamentary committee to discuss the controversy surrounding the purchase of passports.

Speaking at a meeting of the House of Representatives’ State Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Rayi said the prime minister should be called in to clarify the issue.

“The issue of passport procurement that has come out publicly needs to be discussed by inviting the prime minister,” Rayi said.

Rayi also sought clarification from the government over the formation of a separate asset investigation commission under the government, arguing that it could encroach on the jurisdiction of the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority (CIAA).

He also raised questions over reports that CIAA officials were summoned to the Prime Minister’s Office and questioned for around seven hours.

The CIAA is a constitutional body established to investigate corruption and abuse of authority and to maintain checks and balances over the government.

Questions had been raised after reports that aides of Prime Minister Shah kept all CIAA officials at the Prime Minister’s Office for hours and questioned them.

Rayi said the prime minister should provide an explanation to the parliamentary committee regarding the incident.

item.title: Govt planning to allow private sector to collect biometric data of Nepalis abroad
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Pant
item.description:
Kathmandu, August 20 The government is preparing to allow private-sector entities to collect biometric data from Nepali citizens living abroad as part of the passport application process. The provision has been proposed in the Passport (First Amendment) Bill, 2026, registered in the House of Representatives by Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal on July 30. Under the […]

The post Govt planning to allow private sector to collect biometric data of Nepalis abroad appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.
item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

The government is preparing to allow private-sector entities to collect biometric data from Nepali citizens living abroad as part of the passport application process.

The provision has been proposed in the Passport (First Amendment) Bill, 2026, registered in the House of Representatives by Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal on July 30.

Under the proposed amendment, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs would be able to arrange for private companies or other institutions to collect passport applications along with biometric data from Nepalis abroad.

Currently, biometric collection is handled exclusively through government agencies and Nepali diplomatic missions. Nepali citizens applying for passports abroad must generally appear in person at the relevant embassy or consulate to provide their biometric data.

Concerns over sensitive data

The proposed provision has raised concerns among lawmakers over the security and potential misuse of sensitive personal data.

Rastriya Swatantra Party lawmaker Rima Bishwakarma questioned whether the bill provides adequate safeguards against the misuse of biometric data.

She said the bill lacks clear standards for preventing the misuse of sensitive personal data and stressed the need for explicit legal provisions on data security, use, protection and accountability.

Nepali Congress whip Nishkal Rai also raised concerns about who would control citizens’ data if private companies were allowed to collect it.

He questioned what would happen in cases of data misuse, leaks, subcontractor access, transfers to foreign jurisdictions, incorrect identity matching or failure to destroy data when required.

Rai argued that the bill should establish a clear chain of accountability rather than leaving major decisions concerning citizens’ sensitive information to the executive.

Government cites difficulties faced by Nepalis abroad

Foreign Minister Khanal defended the proposed provision, saying it is intended to make passport services more accessible to Nepalis living far from diplomatic missions.

He said Nepal has embassies in only limited locations while Nepalis are increasingly dispersed across different countries. Requiring citizens to travel long distances simply to provide biometric data can impose significant costs and inconvenience.

Khanal cited Australia as an example, noting that Nepal’s embassy is in Canberra while a large Nepali population lives in Sydney. Travelling from Sydney to Canberra for passport-related services can cost hundreds of dollars in airfare alone, in addition to accommodation expenses.

He said similar challenges exist in Europe, where Nepal does not have diplomatic missions in many countries.

“That’s why we have introduced the concept of third-party provision to see whether the service can be made easier,” Khanal said, adding that the ministry is studying possible arrangements with established institutions that already handle similar services internationally.

Bill moves forward

The bill underwent a preliminary discussion in the House of Representatives on August 18. Parliament subsequently approved a proposal to consider the bill, opening a 72-hour window for lawmakers to submit amendments.

The provision allowing private-sector collection of biometric data is expected to receive further scrutiny during clause-by-clause discussions.

The key issue will be whether the government can expand access to passport services without compromising the security and control of citizens’ biometric data.

The post Govt planning to allow private sector to collect biometric data of Nepalis abroad appeared first on OnlineKhabar English News.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

The Department of Major Arts at St. Xavier’s College, Kathmandu, has begun its three-day theatre run of Bichitra Baje. It is a Nepali adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez’s acclaimed short story A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings.​

The first show took place on Thursday at Miller Hall, Loyola Campus, Thapathali.

There will be two more shows on August 21 at 8:30 a.m. and 12:00 p.m., and the final two shows on August 22 at 11:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.

Written by Kritika Koirala and Raunak Karki, two students in the Department of Major Arts, Bichitra Baje sets the story in a Nepali setting. It follows a village that encounters a mysterious old man with wings. As the villagers react to his arrival with curiosity, fear, faith, and exploitation, the play explores kindness, compassion, and how people treat those who are different from them. The story also follows Punam, a young girl who responds to the old man with care and respect.

The production is a student-led initiative, with students taking responsibility for different aspects of the play under their teachers’ guidance and mentorship. From acting and writing to stage preparation and props, students have been actively involved in bringing the production to life. The handmade props, in particular, reflect their creative effort and hands-on involvement. Working together throughout the production has also helped them strengthen their teamwork, coordination, and ability to work as a group.​

This play is part of the students’ academic engagement with drama. It aims to give them practical experience in theatre, while also creating a space for students to develop their confidence, creativity and teamwork.

A special feature of this year’s play is its focus on accessibility. The department has set up live audio descriptions for visually impaired audience members. A volunteer will describe key visual parts of the performance, such as movements, expressions, costumes, and actions, using a live Google Meet session. Earphones and internet access will be provided to help with this service.​

Fr. Dr Augustine Thomas, S.J., Principal of St. Xavier’s College, said, “Bichitra Baje is a remarkable example of how our students can transform a powerful literary work into a meaningful theatrical experience. The play invites us to look beyond appearances and differences and rediscover the value of human dignity. I am proud of our students for using the stage to make us reflect on what it means to be truly human.”

Shishir Kumar Bhusal, Head of the Department of Major Arts, said, “It is so heartwarming to witness the play performed by our students here at St. Xavier’s College. The play, Bichitra Baje, stages why human literacy, empathy, emotional intelligence, and interpersonal communication are significant to discuss in today’s society.”

Kathmandu, August 20

Nepali Congress Vice-President Bishwa Prakash Sharma has urged everyone to become active in strengthening party unity, following the path shown by late leader Pradeep Giri.

Opening the second day of the seventh meeting of the Central Policy, Research and Training Academy, Sharma appealed, urging all to move forward on the path shown by Giri to strengthen party unity.

At the meeting, recalling Giri’s thinking and personality, Academy deputy chief Madhu Acharya and members Dr Gopal Dahit Tharu, Mahendra Yadav, Janak Chataut, Er. Amrit Gyawali, Prakash Lamichhane, Prakriti Bhattarai, Anupa Shrestha, and Congress Lalitpur district president Jitendra Shrestha shared their views.

Acting chief secretary Krishna Prasad Dulal said the ongoing meeting would also discuss preparations for the Women’s Green Run and Women’s Entrepreneurship Conference, along with policy and action plan presentations from various subcommittees.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

Nepal and three other countries have signed an agreement to exchange pre-arrival information on goods at customs.

The Department of Customs said the memorandum of understanding was signed among member countries of the South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation (SASEC) to facilitate trade and strengthen customs controls.

The agreement was signed by the customs administrations of Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and the Maldives during the 14th SASEC Subgroup Meeting held in the Maldives. On behalf of Nepal, Director General of the Department of Customs Yamlal Bhusal signed the agreement.

According to the department, the main objective of the agreement is to facilitate the exchange of pre-arrival information on goods among member countries. This will allow customs authorities to analyse available information and manage risks before goods arrive at customs offices.

The department said the arrangement will help strengthen customs controls and facilitate faster and more efficient clearance of goods. It is also expected to reduce the time and cost involved in trade procedures and make foreign trade more convenient, transparent and predictable.

Nepal and India had previously signed a similar memorandum of understanding. The agreement was signed between the Department of Customs and India’s Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs in New Delhi in the first week of Magh, 2082 BS.

Both countries expect the arrangement to strengthen cooperation between their customs administrations and facilitate risk analysis by exchanging data on goods before their arrival, making it easier to monitor and regulate shipments identified as high-risk.

The system is also expected to provide greater facilitation to compliant businesses and make customs clearance faster and more efficient. Pre-arrival data exchange among major trading partners is an established international practice aimed at facilitating trade through risk management.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) lawmaker Khagendra Sunar has accused middlemen of effectively taking over Nepal Police Headquarters, raising questions over procurement of police equipment.

Speaking at the House of Representatives’ Public Accounts Committee, Sunar asked whether the information the committee had sought from police authorities on procurement had been submitted.

“We had asked for information on police equipment procurement within 15 days. Has it been submitted? Meanwhile, the police have issued tenders worth hundreds of millions of rupees. Certain middlemen have taken over police headquarters,” Sunar said.

Sunar also stood by the questions he raised during the committee’s previous meeting, saying he was prepared to face legal action if anyone felt his remarks had damaged their reputation.

“I stand by the questions I raised and remain firm. If anyone feels their reputation has been harmed, they can go to court. I am ready to answer in the dock,” he said.

He also criticised the Nepal Police leadership for allegedly engaging in a confrontation with him during the committee meeting.

Sunar’s remarks during the previous committee meeting had drawn criticism over his language and conduct. Speaker DP Aryal had subsequently discussed the matter with the committee chair, secretary and Inspector General of Police.

The RSP had also instructed its lawmakers to maintain decorum in their presentations.

item.content:encoded:
Kathmandu, August 20

A police team on regular patrol has arrested two people with more than 660 kilograms of marijuana in Sarlahi district.

According to the Nepal Police newsroom, Nar Bahadur Thing, 63, and Jesun Maya Thing, 52, of Lalbandi Municipality-14 were arrested with 660 kilograms of marijuana on Wednesday.

Police recovered 560 kilograms of marijuana from Nar Bahadur’s house and another 100 kilograms from Jesun Maya’s cowshed.
